_comment: Canonical Fleet Core staffing data — the ONE authoring source for the model palette, the effort vocabulary, the work-shape tier policy, the per-vendor palette, the capability ratings and trust tiers, and the per-role staffing defaults (issue #1021). It absorbs the former models.json and tier_policy.json, which are deleted. models/efforts are the live Claude vocabulary for existing consumers (tier_palette.MODELS/EFFORTS, tier_resolver.resolve()). Do not treat them as the multi-vendor router. scalar_efforts, execution_classes, and root_orchestration_profiles are the portable version-2 subset ported from Codex (KTD7); they are the authoritative execution-class policy. lineage_models/lineage_efforts are Codex compatibility data and are deliberately not ported. work_shapes is the work-shape -> tier registry that tier_resolver.load_policy() reads. vendors is the per-vendor palette that tier_resolver derives SUPPORTED_RUNTIMES, _RUNTIME_MODELS, _RUNTIME_ACCEPTED_EFFORTS, _EFFORT_COLLAPSE and _EFFORT_APPLICATION_MODE from. ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING for models/efforts: rank 0 is the strongest model, rung 0 is the weakest effort. Grow the Claude vocabulary under models/efforts, never with a second bare literal elsewhere — see plugins/fleet-core/references/staffing.md.

judgment.rationale: Judgment, design, adversarial review, architectural decisions — deep reasoning needed; cost-justified.

mechanical.rationale: Mechanical, deterministic, scripted transforms, scaffolding — bounded output, predictable steps.

purely-mechanical.rationale: Purely mechanical work within the mechanical work-shape — cheapest tier still safe for bounded, predictable steps.

read-only-survey.rationale: Read-only survey, search, grep, sampling, census — low-effort read, no write risk.

offload-test-gated.rationale: External-engine delegation, intent=offload, verifiability=test-gated — chaperone ratifies the declared test oracle and provenance; keep the chaperone cheap unless evidence size escalates.

offload.rationale: External-engine delegation, intent=offload, verifiability=unverifiable or absent — chaperone performs full review; a heavier default would erase the token savings that motivated delegation (KTD2).

second-opinion.rationale: External-engine delegation, intent=second-opinion — adversarial verification IS the product; extra spend assumed; fable/xhigh available as a per-unit override, never a default (KTD2).

divergence.rationale: External-engine delegation, intent=divergence — agreement and disagreement are both explicit adversarial-review outcomes; use the high-tier chaperone posture.

_vendors_comment: hermes is the eighth agent kind the agent-launcher skill names in prose, and it is deliberately absent from this palette: the topology table describes it as reconciling a profile workspace and owning its own routing, so there is no model or effort for this component to choose. The vendor keys here are compared as a set against the launcher's VENDOR_FLAGS table, so adding a kind there reds tests/test_staffing.py rather than passing silently.

opencode.unsupported_reason: The launcher can start opencode, but nobody has verified its launch-time effort and model arguments, and its model identifier must be in provider/model form, which no other vendor requires. Promoting it means verifying those arguments on a live host first, then flipping runtime_supported and filling accepted_efforts.

review-max.description: Explicit escalation for unusually ambiguous or high-risk review.

review-high.description: Architecture, security, adversarial, API, privacy, and quality review.

test-medium.description: General workers, testers, and interpretation of ambiguous validator output.

monitor-low.description: Network-aware CI, deploy, and runtime observation.

work-high.description: Complex bounded implementation with declared workspace writes.

work-medium.description: Ordinary implementation, remediation, and Git integration.
